title: Remove duplicate customers
summary: Delete duplicate customer rows by normalised email, keeping the most recently updated one.
prompt: A sign-up bug created duplicate customers. Two rows are the same customer when their emails match
**ignoring case and surrounding spaces** (`' Ana@Example.com '` is `ana@example.com`).
Write a `DELETE` that leaves exactly one row per customer: the one with the latest `updated_at`.
If two duplicates have the same `updated_at`, keep the one with the **higher** `id`.
Do not change the rows you keep.
Table: `customers(id, email, name, updated_at)`; `updated_at` is `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.
The tests look at `SELECT id, email, name FROM customers ORDER BY id` afterwards.
setup: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL);
stateQuery: SELECT id, email, name FROM customers ORDER BY id
solution: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(trim(email)) ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn
wrong: SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM customers
WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM customers GROUP BY lower(trim(email)));
hints: `lower(trim(email))` is the key that groups duplicates.
`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(trim(email)) ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC)` gives the keeper rank 1.
Delete every id whose rank is above 1: `DELETE FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM (...) WHERE rn > 1)`.
